Growth & Social Media — Portfolio

I can tell what's going to spread.

I'm Almontaser Ahmed. I ran growth and content for Loopy, a live-wallpaper app, on Threads and TikTok — and turned two accounts that started at zero into 10,000+ app downloads. Threads went from launch to 30,600 followers, most of it inside the first three months. TikTok went further with less: a 762-follower account put up a 1.1M-view video, because the feed shows a post to strangers when the post earns it. Two platforms, two different games, one skill underneath — knowing which piece of content is going to travel before it's posted. Every screenshot below links to the real, live post.

01

One library, two platforms

Same weekly wallpaper drop, cut two ways: character art plus a phone mockup for Threads, a 9-second reveal clip for TikTok. One production pass, not two.

02

Picking the character is the job

Every post used the same format — one character, one hook, one reveal. The only variable was which character got picked, and that call is where the results came from: Sanji, the newspaper-style Tanjiro and Giyu pair, the Neymar clip that took off on TikTok. None of it was thrown at the wall.

03

Built for each platform's real incentive

Threads rewards showing up every day; TikTok rewards one post landing, whoever posted it. Same library, aimed at two different games — and it scored in both.

04

Measured weekly, doubled down on what worked

Reach, engagement and follower growth got checked every week on both platforms, and the hours followed the returns. When TikTok started paying back more per post, it got more of my time — and delivered the biggest number on this page.

TikTok

@otakupaperz62 — the breakout

762 followers — next to nothing — and still the account's single biggest result: 1.1 million views on one video, 1.89 million across the account. TikTok's feed doesn't check who's posting, only whether a post is worth showing to a stranger. Four separate times it decided the pick was worth it, and every one of those four used the same nine-second reveal format.

Proof of: content curation · discovery-feed targeting · cross-platform repurposing

Reach vs. following
Four different posts on this account cleared thousands of likes each — the 62,300-like Neymar video above plus the three shown here, all in the same nine-second reveal format. The following never had to grow for that to keep happening. When the post itself was right, the feed did the distribution.

Where those 1.89M views actually came from

Views per post across all 47 posts, ranked — log scale, because three posts carried about 82% of the account's total reach. That shape is the point: on TikTok, picking right beats posting more.

Threads

@loopypapers — zero to 30,600

Launched from nothing and built to 30,600 followers — most of it inside the first three months — through daily posting, hook testing and a sharp eye for which characters the audience would rally around. The format kept delivering well beyond the launch push: two of the account's three biggest posts came months later, on a fraction of the posting cadence. I ran four Threads accounts for the company in total, which is where I learned to read platform rules and risk as carefully as engagement numbers.

Proof of: content curation · community building · platform-risk management

Why it matters
Three months of focused work built a 30,000-strong audience from nothing, and the format kept producing long after — six posts over a thousand likes, with two of the three biggest arriving months after launch. A format that keeps scoring on a lighter cadence is a format with a lot of headroom left in it.

What this shows

Two platforms, four accounts, one person, all of it built in under a year. Here's what it shows.

01

The instinct is the transferable part

TikTok's best video came from an account with 762 followers. The feed didn't care who was posting, only whether the pick was right — and that judgment call is the same one behind every post on this page. It moves with me to any brand, any platform.

02

Threads shows it's repeatable

Six posts over a thousand likes, a 30,600-strong following built in months, and hits that kept landing well after launch. Same eye for content, different platform, same result.

03

All of it with one person and no budget

Every number on this page came from organic content — no paid push, no agency, no team. Four accounts, two platforms and a launch-to-30,000 curve, run solo alongside a full-time internship. That's the baseline, not the ceiling.

04

What I'd do with a real runway

Give the same eye for content a proper plan, a small budget and a second pair of hands, and the numbers on this page become the floor. Picking what travels is the hard part, and it's the part I've already shown. That's the conversation I'd like to have.
